problem: Use the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{7}$ in ascending powers of $x$ to approximate $(0.99)^{7}.$ Give your answer to four decimal places.
worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{1}{2!}n(n-1){x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{7} & =1+7x+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot {x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{7} \\  & =1+7x+21{x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{7}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(1+x)}^{7}≈1+7x+21{x}^{2}.
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=-0.01$ into the above approximation of $(1+x)^{7}:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}(0.99)^{7} & =(1+(-0.01))^{7} \\  & ≈1+7(-0.01)+21(-0.01)^{2} \\  & =1-7(0.01)+21(0.000\,1) \\  & =1-0.07+0.002\,1 \\  & =0.932\,1,\end{aligned}
$$

to four decimal places.
